definitions.explanation: A shop that sells fresh meat.
A person who sells meat at a shop.

examples.english: I bought it at the butcher shop.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{肉屋|にくや}はコロッケが{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: The butcher shop in front of the station is famous for its croquettes.

examples.japanese: この{辺|あた}りには{昔|むかし}ながらの{肉屋|にくや}がまだ{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: There are still old-fashioned butcher shops remaining in this area.

examples.japanese: {肉屋|にくや}のおじさんが{親切|しんせつ}だ。
{肉屋|にくや}に{薄切|うすぎ}りにしてもらった。
examples.english: I had the butcher slice it thin.

examples.japanese: {肉屋|にくや}に{相談|そうだん}したら、すき{焼|や}きには{肩|かた}ロースがいいと{勧|すす}められた。
examples.english: When I asked the butcher, he recommended chuck roll for sukiyaki.

notes:
FORMATION: {肉|にく} (meat) + {屋|や} (shop/person). The suffix {屋|や} can refer to both the shop and the shopkeeper.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肉屋|にくや}で{買|か}う: to buy at a butcher shop
- {肉屋|にくや}のコロッケ: butcher shop croquettes (a classic Japanese takeaway item)
- {町|まち}の{肉屋|にくや}: neighborhood butcher shop

CULTURE: Traditional {肉屋|にくや} in Japan often sell ready-made fried items like croquettes (コロッケ) and {串|くし}カツ alongside raw meat. Many neighborhoods still have independent butcher shops, though supermarkets have become the primary place to buy meat.
